ky_bruise_brothers_wall.blurb: A compact sandstone wall on the floor of Muir Valley, mostly sport with a handful of trad lines. The climbing is on the gentler side of the valley's offerings: most lines are vertical or a touch less than vertical rather than overhanging, with plenty of 5.8 through 5.10 and a smaller group of 5.11s and 5.12s at the top end. Overseer, Beta Babes and Return of Manimal are among the favorites. The walk in is easy and mostly flat after the initial descent, which makes this a good first stop for newer leaders working up through the grades.
ky_bruise_brothers_wall.parking_note: Leave the car in the main Muir Valley lot; the trailheads for both valley paths sit behind the pavilion at the back of that lot. The wall is reached from the South path.
ky_bruise_brothers_wall.approach: From the main lot take the South trail behind the barn down into the valley. At the bottom turn right, cross the bridge, then follow the wide old logging road uphill past the Sunnyside fork. The left end of the wall is a few minutes further, with the main face about a hundred feet beyond.

ky_velo_crag.blurb: A sandstone crag in Flat Hollow, in the southern part of the Pendergrass-Murray preserve. The walls are mostly vertical, with sport routes making up most of the climbing and a few trad lines mixed in. Grades run from easy up through the low 5.12s, with a solid core of 5.10s and 5.11s, so it suits a party with a range of abilities. The Century, Lightning Rod Arete and Thunderface are among the standouts. The face gets shade in the morning and sun later in the day, and a short pinnacle section to one side adds some variety.
ky_velo_crag.parking_note: Park in the Flat Hollow lot of the Pendergrass-Murray preserve.
ky_velo_crag.approach: From the Flat Hollow lot walk back toward the entrance and take a sharp right up the old oil road. Follow it to where it ends, then pick up the short trail marked by a Velo sign to reach the base of the wall. Steps lead to the left side; the right side is reached along the base of the cliff.

ky_neverland.blurb: One of the newer crags in the Miller Fork preserve, sitting across the hollow from Camelot. It is mostly sport climbing on sandstone, with a large block of 5.10s and a good number of easier lines as well, and a few 5.11s for those wanting a bit more. One sector is a good spot for people just starting to lead. Because the routes have not seen heavy traffic, some rock is still loose or brittle, so a helmet is a sensible choice. Fairydust, One Feeling, Walk the Plank and Hook are the lines to start with.
ky_neverland.parking_note: Use the big gravel lot of the Miller Fork preserve, off KY 11 by way of Shoemaker Ridge Road and then Hell Creek Road. The final stretch beside the river is rough, so a high-clearance vehicle is wise.
ky_neverland.approach: Take the Miller East trail over the footbridge and follow the Camelot approach. Roughly a hundred yards before that trail swings uphill and right, bear left, cross a stream, and walk through the floodplain toward a huge boulder. When the trail turns uphill, a short run of switchbacks reaches the base.

ky_dark_side_the.blurb: Steep, pocket-riddled sandstone the color of slate, tucked into Coal Bank Hollow and known as one of the Red's top spots for hard sport climbing. The face bulges at a sustained angle, and some routes have huecos big enough to rest in. There are 5.13s in abundance and a healthy number of 5.12s, while easy and moderate climbing is scarce, so it is a place for projecting rather than warming up. The wall sits in shade through the day and most lines stay dry when it rains. Many route names follow a Star Wars theme, among them The Force, Elephant Man and Tuskan Raider.
ky_dark_side_the.parking_note: From KY 11 take Fixer Road. The pavement gives way to dirt after a few houses, and about a mile along you turn right opposite a large tank beside the road. The lot with the information kiosk is at the end of that track.
ky_dark_side_the.approach: From the kiosk a trail crosses the creek and heads up the hollow past the signed turns for Gold Coast and Solar Collector. Switchbacks climb a steep hill, then bear right at the first boulder to reach the left end of the wall.

ky_camelot.blurb: A sandstone wall in the Miller Fork preserve with a strong selection of moderate routes, mostly sport and with a handful of trad lines. The grades start around 5.5 and work up to 5.12, with the greatest weight in the 5.8 to 5.10 range, so there is something for newer leaders and for people warming up for harder things. Holy Grail, Lady of the Lake, Roger the Shrubber and She's a Witch are the lines most people come for. The route names follow an Arthurian theme. The approach crosses a floodplain and a creek, so expect wet feet after rain.
ky_camelot.parking_note: Use the big gravel lot of the Miller Fork preserve, off KY 11 by way of Shoemaker Ridge Road and then Hell Creek Road. The final stretch beside the river is rough, so a high-clearance vehicle is wise.
ky_camelot.approach: From the lot cross the main bridge and follow the trail to the right. At the signed junction toward Corner Pocket turn right, then continue past Corner Pocket up stone steps and switchbacks. Cross a creek and the floodplain, follow the old roadbed left into a hollow, and look for the Camelot sign marking the trail up to the wall.

ky_torrent_falls_limited_access.blurb: A sandstone sport-climbing venue in the Natural Bridge part of the Red River Gorge, just off KY 11 south of Natural Bridge State Resort Park, near a waterfall and an old resort property. The climbing is almost all sport, steep enough to reward strong fingers, with the bulk of the routes between 5.10 and 5.12. Separate sections are known by the grade they hold, such as the 5.10 Wall and the 5.11 Wall, with an amphitheater between them. Centerfire, Steelworker, Bare Metal Teen and Racer X are among the better-known lines.

ky_unlode_the.blurb: A popular sandstone sport crag in the Bald Rock preserve that has been developed heavily in recent years. The routes tackle overhanging jug-pulling of the kind the Red is famous for, but at friendlier grades than the neighboring Motherlode: roughly 5.9 through 5.11, with the largest groups at 5.10 and 5.11. It works well for a first outing on Red sandstone. The wall catches sun in the morning and falls into shade by afternoon. Untoward, Undermined, Untenable and Unrealistic Dump Truck are good places to start, and fall weekends can bring a crowd.
ky_unlode_the.parking_note: Use the designated parking for the Motherlode in the Bald Rock preserve, down the steep Lode hill. That hill is rough, so a high-clearance four-wheel-drive is best; otherwise park at the top and carpool, since space is tight there.
ky_unlode_the.approach: From the Motherlode parking walk back up the hill and along the road for a couple of minutes. Turn onto a heavily overgrown old road on the left, cross the drainage, then look for a cairn and head uphill. The wall is on your right.

ky_real_deep_end.blurb: A secluded wall in the Miller Fork preserve reached by a steep old oil road. Most of the climbing is sport on sandstone, with some trad lines and a single boulder problem, and the grades are centered on 5.9 through 5.11 with a few 5.12s and 5.13s above that. Parts of the wall still carry lichen and some loose rock that should clean up with traffic, so go carefully. An obvious offwidth crack in a left-facing corner marks the main project wall. Castaway and Red Means Go are among the lines to try.

ky_boneyard_the.blurb: A sandstone wall on the south side of Muir Valley that faces north, which makes it a reasonable option in warm weather. The rock is gray and grippy, even a little sharp in places. Climbs are mostly slabby with a cruxy start and easier pocket pulling above, plus a few steeper overhanging lines. Grades run from 5.6 to 5.12, with the heaviest concentration at 5.11. It sits beside the much harder Midnight Surf, so strong parties often stop here to warm up. Bangers and Mash, Trouble in Paradise and Captain Blondie Sinks The Ship are among the best known.
ky_boneyard_the.parking_note: Leave the car in the main Muir Valley lot; the trailheads for both valley paths sit behind the pavilion at the back of that lot.

ky_cove_the.blurb: A cliff-band bouldering area on sandstone above KY 77 near the Nada Tunnel, in the northern Red River Gorge. It holds a few dozen problems that cover a wide spread, with a cluster around V4 to V7 and a serious hard end running from V8 up to V11. A big, heavily chalked roof is the centerpiece. Fame and Money, Drugs and Alcohol, Hobbies Delight and The UFO are among the best-known problems. The walk to the boulders is a steady uphill on a faint trail.
ky_cove_the.approach: From the road a faint trail climbs steeply for roughly ten to fifteen minutes. Pass the first overhang, which holds big boulders and shows no chalk, and continue to the right into the Cove itself, where the roof is heavily chalked.
